view.agent_interpretation: The thesis splits in two. The US power leg is real: data centres are nearly half of US electricity demand growth to 2030 (IEA) and listed power producers hold direct AI offtake contracts, and power equipment is supply-constrained. But it is not overlooked: those stocks fell more than 20% on the DeepSeek day and trade as high-beta AI proxies. The copper leg is the reverse: liquid, leverageable and not crowded, but data-centre copper (about 512 kt, roughly 2% of total demand) is a small slice of the market and ICSG sees refined surpluses through 2027, so copper looks like weak AI exposure; its share of copper demand growth (not total demand) is not yet established. As framed (simple, overlooked AI exposure via energy and copper) the claim is weak; a narrower thesis on supply-constrained US power and grid equipment is better supported but already priced as AI beta.

Needs a grounded growth denominator before this can be judged (open task).

research_updates.summary: Power-side supply is tight: IEA says transformer and cable wait times doubled in three years and gas-turbine deliveries face multi-year lead times; GE Vernova has gas agreements signed into 2031. Copper is tight only on BNEF's long horizon (6 Mt shortfall by 2035); ICSG (Oct 2026) sees refined surpluses of ~104 kt in 2026 and ~368 kt in 2027. The constraint, and so the pricing power, sits in power equipment and generation, not near-term copper. [research worker w-5816eee86ccb]
